notes: First-ever GMT-Master (1954); red/blue bakelite bezel insert, prone to cracking. Bezel color is sometimes disputed for the earliest examples.
Same reference as above; nickname from association with early James Bond films (Sean Connery era).
The most iconic vintage GMT reference (1959-1980); red/blue anodized aluminum bezel insert.
Two-tone steel/gold variant of the 1675 with brown/gold bezel insert.
Transitional reference (1981-1988) adding a quickset date movement; kept acrylic crystal and matte dial; red/blue bezel option.
Two-tone steel/gold GMT-Master with brown/gold bezel insert, produced alongside the 16750.
Same reference as Root Beer above; alternate nickname tied to the actor being photographed wearing one.
Full 18k yellow gold version with brown/gold bezel insert.
Also called 'Sophia Loren'; transitional 1983-1988 reference with a noticeably thicker case and crown guards to fit the new movement; bridges GMT-Master to GMT-Master II design.
Same reference as Fat Lady; red/black bezel insert, the first Rolex GMT with this colorway.
Produced 1999-2007 with aluminum insert; factory option alongside black and Coke bezels. Aluminum fades over time (uneven 'ghost' fading is common).
Same base reference as above with red/black aluminum bezel insert instead of Pepsi; discontinued 2007, no ceramic successor released as of 2026.
Introduced 2013; first bi-color (black/blue) Cerachrom ceramic bezel Rolex ever made. Produced only on Oyster bracelet.
2019 update to the black/blue ceramic GMT with new case and caliber 3285; 'Batman' nickname generally applies to the Oyster-bracelet version of this reference.

Identical reference/bezel to the 2019 Batman above but delivered on a Jubilee bracelet; collectors distinguish 'Batman' vs 'Batgirl' by bracelet, not by a different reference suffix, which causes frequent confusion in listings.
2018 reintroduction of the ceramic Pepsi bezel; Rolex solved the two-color ceramic manufacturing problem that had kept Pepsi out of the ceramic GMT lineup since 2007.
18k white gold case with a genuine Gibeon meteorite dial and Pepsi ceramic bezel; each dial is unique due to natural Widmanstätten pattern.
Green/black Cerachrom bezel in Oystersteel; uses the 'destro' layout with crown at 9 o'clock.
Also called 'Green Hornet'; white gold destro GMT pairing the green/black Sprite bezel with a green dial (borrows the 'Hulk' green-dial association from the Submariner line).
2024 release in Oystersteel with a black/grey Cerachrom bezel; nicknamed after Batman's civilian alter ego since it shares the case/bracelet of the Batman but with a grey instead of blue half.

Yellow Rolesor (steel/yellow gold two-tone) version with the same black/grey Cerachrom bezel as the Bruce Wayne; nicknamed for its dark/light two-tone resemblance to a poured stout. 'GRNR' reportedly abbreviates the French 'Gris Noir' (grey/black).
Modern two-tone Oystersteel/Everose gold GMT with brown/black Cerachrom bezel, reviving the vintage Root Beer colorway in ceramic.
Full 18k Everose gold version of the modern Root Beer, brown/black Cerachrom bezel.
2003-2010, released for the Submariner's 50th anniversary; first Submariner with a green bezel (green anodized aluminum insert, black dial).
2010-2020; full green ceramic bezel paired with a matching green dial (some early/transitional examples had black dials).
Also informally 'Cermit'; replaced the Hulk in 2020 with a 41mm case, green Cerachrom bezel, and a black (not green) sunray dial.
18k white gold case with blue ceramic bezel and matching vivid blue dial.
18k white gold, same blue ceramic bezel as the Smurf but paired with a black dial instead of blue.
Two-tone steel/yellow gold Submariner Date with blue ceramic bezel and blue dial; vintage two-tone blue Subs (e.g. 16613) share the nickname informally.
1950s reference with an oversized 8mm winding crown and no crown guards; famously worn by Sean Connery in early Bond films (Dr. No, etc.).
Military-issued variant supplied to the British Ministry of Defence (fixed lug bars, sword hands on early issues, no date).
Alternate military-issue reference alongside the 5513, supplied to UK armed forces.
Produced roughly 1967-1975/77; early production had 'SUBMARINER' printed in red in the dial's four-line text, giving rise to the nickname. Later runs reverted to white text.
Vintage nickname for certain 5513 dial variants where the Rolex coronet logo's stubby shape is said to resemble the cartoon character's hair.

Special editions supplied to the French diving company COMEX (Compagnie Maritime d'Expertises); helium escape valve equipped. Other Rolex references (1665 Sea-Dweller, 16660, 5513) were also issued to COMEX, but 5514 is the dedicated Submariner COMEX reference.
Vintage 'exotic dial' Daytona with Art Deco-style numerals and contrasting sub-dials; nicknamed after the actor/racer who was photographed wearing one.
Same reference; 'Solo' refers to a dial variant printed with only 'Rolex' (no 'Oyster' or 'Cosmograph' text).
Sister reference to the 6239 with an acrylic (Plexiglas) bezel insert instead of a metal one; also came with exotic dials.
Black dial/black bezel gold-case variant of the 6241, nicknamed after the black-and-gold livery of the John Player Special F1 racing team.
Vintage screw-down pusher Daytona with a large red 'DAYTONA' inscription above the 6 o'clock sub-dial; some 6263 examples also carry Paul Newman exotic dials.

Refers to 6263 (and 16520, see below) examples whose originally silver/white sub-dials have oxidized to a brown/tropical tone; named after auctioneer Osvaldo Patrizzi who popularized these examples at auction.
Same 'Big Red' inscription styling as the 6263, in the otherwise very similar 6265 reference.
Nickname for 6263/6265 dial variants with noticeably oversized sub-dials compared to standard production.
A one-of-a-kind white gold Daytona 6265 with black dial, believed to be a unique factory prototype; sold at Phillips auction in 2018 for over $5 million.
First automatic Daytona (1988-2000), using a modified Zenith El Primero-based caliber 4030 movement rather than an in-house Rolex caliber.
Zenith Daytona examples with sub-dials that have oxidized from silver to a warm brown color due to a manufacturing/lacquer defect; highly sought after despite (or because of) the defect.
Current-shape (2016-2023) steel Daytona with white dial, black sub-dials, and black ceramic bezel.
Same reference with a black dial (black sub-dials) instead of white, giving an all-black look; nickname is more informal/dealer-driven than 'Panda'.
2023-generation successor to the 116500LN with an updated caliber 4131 movement; white dial with black sub-dials and black ceramic bezel.
Black-dial version of the current-generation steel ceramic-bezel Daytona.
18k yellow gold Daytona with a green dial; nickname comes from musician/collector John Mayer publicly favoring and popularizing this combination.
Updated yellow gold green-dial Daytona with the new caliber 4131 and gold (rather than black) sub-dial accents.
2023 release commemorating 100 years of the 24 Hours of Le Mans; reverse-panda dial, square sub-dial markers, black ceramic bezel with a red '100' tachymeter marking.
18k white gold Daytona on an Oysterflex strap sharing the Le Mans reverse-panda dial styling in a different metal/strap combination.
18k yellow gold Daytona with a tiger's-eye gemstone dial and diamond-set bezel; a controversial, less universally loved gem-set model among purist collectors.
18k Everose gold Daytona with a rainbow-gradient sapphire bezel and baguette sapphire hour markers.
Updated Everose gold Rainbow Daytona with caliber 4131.
18k yellow gold Daytona on an Oysterflex strap with a bright yellow/gold dial; nicknamed for the resemblance to the Pokemon character's color.
Updated caliber-4131 version of the yellow-dial gold Daytona on Oysterflex.
Italian for 'arrow'; first Explorer II (1971-1985), recognizable for its oversized orange 24-hour arrow-tipped GMT hand.
Same reference as the Freccione; popular nickname despite disputed/unconfirmed evidence that McQueen actually owned or wore one - included here as a widely used (if contested) collector nickname.
White-dial version of the 1989-2011 Explorer II, black-outlined hour markers/hands contrasting with the white dial.
42mm (2011-2021) white-dial Explorer II continuing the Polar nickname.

Slate-grey sunray dial with green-outlined Roman numerals, resembling grass-court tennis branding; name is entirely collector/dealer-coined, never used officially by Rolex. Sibling references 126234, 126233, 126333 share the same dial and nickname.
1970s-80s Datejust with hand-painted (rather than applied) Roman numerals, named after the dial-painting workshop/style.
Datejust Turn-O-Graph with a rotating engine-turned timing bezel; 'Thunderbird' name traces to a 1950s association with the U.S. Air Force Thunderbirds demonstration team.
Late-1960s/1970s Day-Date with unusually wide/thick baton hour markers and hands compared to standard production.
Also called 'Puzzle' or 'Jigsaw'; 2023 Day-Date 36 with a champleve-enamel dial made of interlocking colorful puzzle-piece motifs.

The original 1972 Gerald Genta-designed Royal Oak; 39mm case was large for its era (ultra-thin automatic caliber 2121). 'Jumbo' became the retroactive nickname once smaller Royal Oak models were introduced and a shorthand was needed.
The original 1993 Royal Oak Offshore, 42mm; considered oversized/aggressive for its time versus the standard Royal Oak, earning the nickname at launch.
2003 titanium Offshore with thick lugs and bold black dial; nicknamed for being worn by Arnold Schwarzenegger in Terminator 3: Rise of the Machines.

Introduced 2005; cream/ivory Mega Tapisserie dial paired with a brown hornback alligator strap (the only Offshore fitted with this strap), giving rise to the 'Safari' name. Discontinued when the Offshore line was redesigned in 2014.
Third-generation (straight-lug) pre-Professional Speedmaster worn by NASA astronaut Ed White during the first American spacewalk on Gemini 4 (1965); powered by caliber 321.
2020 reissue reviving the straight-lug case and manual-wind caliber 321 movement of the original Ed White reference, for the 50th anniversary of Apollo 11/13-era production.

Current standard-production Speedmaster Professional with hesalite crystal and caliber 1861/3861; 'Moonwatch' is the generic nickname for this lineage tracing to NASA qualification and the Apollo 11 moon landing.
Speedmaster Racing Co-Axial with white dial and contrasting black sub-dials (caliber 3330), following the black/white 'panda dial' convention shared with the Rolex Daytona.
2003 limited edition (300 pieces) of the Speedmaster Professional made for Japan's Mitsukoshi department store, with a white panda-style dial and black sub-dials.

2008 limited edition (1,970 pieces) commemorating Omega's late-1960s/70s 'Alaska Project' - a secret NASA-adjacent program to develop an extreme-temperature-resistant chronograph; features a red aluminum outer case and red accents.
'Speedy Tuesday 2' limited edition (2,012 pieces) inspired by the orange-accented Speedmaster from the Japanese TV series Return of Ultraman; UV-reactive Ultraman artwork on the 9 o'clock sub-dial.

Seamaster Diver 300M with blue wave dial worn by Pierce Brosnan as James Bond in GoldenEye (1995); the film placement launched Omega's long-running Bond partnership and gave this generation of the model its enduring nickname.
